facility_roles.note: Start = the first demonstration runs at LNGS; the underground emulsion-handling facility (hall F) was built after the 2016 letter of intent. Open: see the interval note.
facility_roles.quote: Several demonstration runs of the NEWSdm experiment were conducted at LNGS from 2021 to 2022 as a proof-of-principle.

intervals.label: NEWS letter of intent to LNGS and emulsion-facility construction
intervals.note: Start = the arXiv posting of the letter of intent (LNGS-LOI 48/15, 14 April 2016); the LOI proposes a one-kilogram pilot experiment at LNGS. End = the first demonstration runs (2021). After the LOI a new emulsion-handling facility was constructed in the LNGS underground laboratory (ICHEP 2022 proceedings). No approval date is published in the sources read.

intervals.label: demonstration and pilot runs at LNGS (equatorial-telescope run in progress in 2024)
intervals.note: Start verified (2021). Open interval: the ICHEP 2024 contribution (July 2024) says 'a run with equatorial telescope is in progress'; no later source was found. These are proof-of-principle and pilot runs, not the full-scale experiment.
intervals.quote: Several demonstration runs of the NEWSdm experiment were conducted at LNGS from 2021 to 2022 as a proof-of-principle.

notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
Added as a comparable directional experiment: the bar is met by the published 2023 limit and by the LNGS location (demonstration runs and a facility in the underground laboratory).

The 2023 directional limit came from an exposure at the ground floor of a building at Nagoya University (sea level), not at LNGS; facility_ids is empty on that result. No facility record for Nagoya exists.
Official website news-dm.lngs.infn.it (named on conference slides) did not respond; links.website stays null.

physics_goals.quote: We propose here the use of a detector based on nuclear emulsions to measure the direction of WIMP-induced nuclear recoils.
physics_goals.value: Directional detection of WIMP dark matter with nuclear emulsions

summary.plain: NEWSdm is a directional dark matter project that uses nuclear emulsion, a photographic film with nanometre-sized grains, to record the tiny tracks of recoiling nuclei. The film sits on a telescope mount that follows the sky. Prototype runs are done at Gran Sasso; a first limit from a surface exposure appeared in 2023.
summary.technical: NEWSdm (Nuclear Emulsions for WIMP Search with directional measurement): Nano Imaging Tracker (NIT) super-fine-grained emulsion films, ~100 nm track recording, read with optical microscopy and machine-learning selection, exposed inside a shield on an equatorial telescope mount that cancels Earth rotation. Emulsion produced underground in LNGS hall F; demonstration runs 2021-2022 with the shield in hall C. 2023: first direction-sensitive limit from a surface exposure (39 days, 0.59 g d, Nagoya).
